body:
## User outcome

Provide one reproducible GA4GH test API for SDK, CLI and browser-client authors, with controllable asynchronous behavior and failures. Use the same versioned scenario service locally, in CI and in optional isolated hosted sessions.

Existing [proTES fake TES](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/proTES/blob/55c4d1591cd3be883ad0b4fd2da01d49976414cb/tests/smoke/fake_tes.py), [DRS compliance mocks](https://github.com/ga4gh/drs-compliance-suite), [test runners](https://github.com/ga4gh/openapi-test-runner/blob/bc3eb911e877521409348e0225852d072d4de196/README.md) and [Reference Cloud](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-reference-cloud/blob/d014815b06331ab0843c3ec222b5f74ef964722e/DESIGN.md) are foundations. The new deliverable is a shared client-facing product with scenario control, isolation and cross-client adoption.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Publish an OCI image and a small language-neutral scenario pack with pinned OpenAPI revisions. Begin with TES lifecycle and WES multipart; add minimal DRS/TRS fixtures needed for one complete client flow.
- [ ] Separate the scenario control API from GA4GH routes. It allocates/reset sessions, selects a seed, advances transitions or logical time, and exposes a sanitized event journal. No SDK-private models are required.
- [ ] Support consistent create/get/list/cancel identities and named faults: accepted submission with lost response, cancellation/completion race, bounded 429/503, opaque paging, DRS 202/Retry-After and expiring artifact access.
- [ ] Mark each case as normative behavior, a provider-specific profile or intentional malformed/failure input. A deliberately broken server response must not become a conformance requirement.
- [ ] Parse real WES multipart data and serve real binary fixtures where needed. Generic OpenAPI-generated JSON examples alone are insufficient for these cases.
- [ ] Run the same WES scenarios against the SDK and the maintained [RestWesProvider](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/cloud-components/blob/44c6f96fbfbeff6892ba0ca3836a7bcbd7c9069a/packages/ecc-client-ga4gh-wes/src/providers/rest-wes-provider.ts). Use existing [SDK #5](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/issues/5)/[#15](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-sdk/issues/15) and [cloud-components #484](https://github.com/elixir-cloud-aai/cloud-components/issues/484) as adoption points.
- [ ] Two concurrent sessions cannot inspect or reset each other's state. The same ordered control events and seed reproduce responses; this does not promise identical operating-system thread scheduling or packet timing.
- [ ] Export a replay bundle containing image/spec/pack digests, seed, synthetic request inputs and sanitized events. Reproduce a lost-response case locally and count accepted simulated tasks.

## Hosted stage

Coordinate with [Reference Cloud #34](https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-reference-cloud/issues/34) to offer ephemeral fault-testing sessions using the same image, with server-enforced expiry, quotas and documented browser CORS. Accept only synthetic fixtures: submitted containers are not executed and arbitrary submitted URLs are not fetched. CI can pin a local image instead of relying on public uptime.

## Boundaries and overlap

Static fixtures remain useful for decoding and documentation. The stateful simulator verifies client protocol behavior. Actual staging, execution, cancellation cleanup and scientific outputs require real backends.

Reuse established HTTP/fault machinery and existing mocks rather than building a new generic mocking framework or compliance runner. Replay export belongs here, not in another project. Preserve implementation-specific proTES fixtures where extraction would erase their intended behavior.

## Linked work

- https://github.com/ga4gh/drs-compliance-suite/issues/25
- https://github.com/ga4gh/openapi-test-runner/issues/80
- https://github.com/ga4gh/ga4gh-reference-cloud/issues/34

## F1 — Typed Web API v2 client + fixture-driven mock adapter

### Goal
On top of merged C0 [PR #8](https://github.com/Pickle-Pee/smm_ai_helper_web/pull/8), prepare Next.js frontend for FastAPI Web API v2 while **keeping production/default behavior strictly mock-only**, without any real API/AI requests, auth claims, backend changes, DNS/Caddy/Docker changes, or deployment changes.

### Baseline
- frontend `main` after merged PR #3 (design), #5 (Brenvio deploy), #8 (C0)
- canonical contract: `docs/api/web-api-v2.openapi.yaml`; 65 fixtures indexed in `docs/api/fixtures/index.json`, including stale-receipt recovery golden case
- existing UI boundaries: `lib/api/contracts.ts` (current read-only UI `ApiClient`), `lib/api/mock-client.ts`, `lib/api/provider.tsx`, `features/projects/store.tsx`, `features/workspace/store.tsx` (local-only mutations), `features/workspace/WorkspaceView.tsx`

### Deliverables
1. Lock `openapi-typescript` as devDependency, deterministic generated types under `lib/api/generated/` (or equivalent); `generate:api` and CI drift validation. No manually duplicated DTOs.
2. Typed **WebApiV2Client** with same-origin `/api/v2`, injected `fetch`, `credentials: same-origin`, JSON decoding and typed discriminated errors; CSRF on unsafe methods once session exists, no browser bot token or Telegram identity headers; abort/timeout, explicit 401/403/404/409/429/503, HTML/empty 502/504 support. No automatic AI POST retries; recovery by identical `request_key` on GET, consistent with safe seven-day pending rule and backend authority. HTTP client may be tested against fake fetch but **must not be selected in production or send live requests**.
3. **FixtureWebApiV2Client** with deterministic stateful test scenarios: auth projection, org/project/brand, copilot threads, clarifications/revisions, pending/running/completed, 503 recovery, ambiguous, expired, stale receipt (31 days must not regenerate), snapshots (`presentation.payload`), quota and access denial. Any example content in UI is explicitly marked “Пример из тестовых данных”, never a generated AI answer.
4. Adapter/presenters translating generated Web DTO to existing `lib/types.ts` UI types, preserving all current routes and local-only behavior, handling unsupported capabilities as disabled rather than inventing server writes. No false persistence; preserve existing PreviewBanner, noindex, responsive design.
5. Unit and contract tests for DTO discriminators, response normalization, retry/idempotency, per-viewer `is_self`, snapshots and cross-tenant error behavior; contract checker `python docs/api/tools/check_contract.py` in CI, deterministic TS codegen drift check. Existing `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, hardened Docker smoke continue passing.
6. README with mock-vs-HTTP boundaries and future switch-on prerequisites (backend B1–B6, auth/session, edge F4, security testing, product/ops decisions). Separate small **Draft PR** against current `main`. Do not merge or enable HTTP mode.

### Non-negotiable
- Do not touch backend repo / real FastAPI API; C0 endpoints are **proposed**, not implemented.
- No code that makes browser requests to `/api/v2` from the deployed preview or silently activates HTTP mode via env.
- No fake AI success, no fake remote persistence, no touching production services.
- Web chat = future; documents still mock-only.
- No new projects model redefinition: existing UI read-only `ApiClient` and local reducers must remain compatible; new typed v2 transport can be separate and adapter-injected.
- No auto retry of a model call on 503/ambiguous/expired/receipt missing. Old pending after 30-day retention never resubmitted by the frontend.
- If the broader scope is too large, prioritize codegen + HTTP transport + fixture client + tests; defer large UI modifications to F2.

### Acceptance
Draft PR, pass checks, precise file list, demonstrated mock-only behavior on both desktop and mobile, generated types + contract validation, zero real network calls to proposed API during smoke/production. Link architecture #6 and C0 #7.
title: [F1] Typed Web API v2 client and fixture-driven mock integration (no live backend)

## Destination

A settled test architecture for everything Ynot does against the YNAB API, ready to hand to `/opal:new` as a spec: how the API is mocked at each layer of the pyramid, how a consumer-driven contract keeps the mock honest against real YNAB, and how a generated dataset is seeded into a test budget for integration tests.

_Proposed by Claude on 2026-10-17; Jamie to confirm or redraw._

## Notes

- Domain: the Ynot repo (static browser app, no backend, PAT auth). Money is YNAB milliunits (ADR 0005); memo safety and resending `approved` (ADR 0007); 200 requests per hour per token.
- Already in place: the hand-written stateful fake `test/fakeYnab.ts` (unit tests via `fetchImpl`, Playwright via `page.route`), the e2e fixture budget in `e2e/fixtures.ts`, fast-check arbitraries in `test/arbitraries.ts`, and the contract-check harness `scripts/contract-checks.ts` (PR #27) that probes five undocumented behaviours on the owner's test budget.
- The gap this map closes: nothing proves the fake behaves like YNAB, the contract checks are a one-off script rather than a contract, and there is no way to put a known dataset into a real budget.
- Skills: `/research` for research tickets, `/prototype` for prototype tickets, `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` otherwise.
- Constraint: the contract-check and task 9 branches (PRs #27 and #28) are owned by another thread; build on them, don't change them.
- Research notes and the seeding prototype are in PR #37.

## Decisions so far

- [What can the YNAB API create, change and delete to seed a test budget?](https://github.com/jeasmith/ynot/issues/30) — everything but the plan and a few states (closed accounts, hidden categories); the test plan is long-lived and reseeded idempotently by `import_id`; nine behaviours need contract checks.
- [How do consumer-driven contracts work when the provider won't verify them?](https://github.com/jeasmith/ynot/issues/31) — not Pact or bi-directional; one TypeScript conformance suite run against both the fake and the real API, with optional schema validation.
- [Which mocking approach should back each test layer?](https://github.com/jeasmith/ynot/issues/32) — keep the hand-written fake everywhere networked; add Node-only OpenAPI validation inside it; no MSW or Prism.

## Not yet specified

- **Resetting the test budget between runs.** Research points to a long-lived plan reset in place by bulk PATCH on `import_id`, since a full delete costs one request per transaction. Still open: what a run may change, and how a failed run is cleaned up.
- **Generated data at scale.** Large property-based or volume datasets (thousands of transactions, the 30 second timeout, date windowing) for performance and loader tests; shape depends on the seeding prototype.
- **Watching for YNAB API drift.** How a new OpenAPI version (`openapi/ynab-1.87.0.yaml`) or a changed behaviour is noticed: a diff, a scheduled verification, or both.
- **Playwright against the real budget.** Whether a small number of e2e journeys also run against the seeded budget, and how they would avoid writing to anything but the seeded data.

## Out of scope

- Testing YNAB itself, or load testing against the real API.
title: Map: testing infrastructure for the YNAB API

| Prioridade | Critério |
| --- | --- |
| **P0-crítico** | Segurança, bugs e base de desempenho para operar como serviço público. Fazer primeiro |
| **P1-alto** | Mínimo para competir com o mercado e lançar o plano pago |
| **P2-médio** | Diferenciais do plano Pro |
| **P3-baixo** | Plano Team e evolução futura |

## Approved decisions (maintainer, 2026-11-05)

1. **A purpose-built, stateful GitHub API emulator backed by real git over HTTPS:** option D below. Emulate and WireMock are not adopted.
2. **A production-grade `ca_bundle` option, one per origin**, with strict validation and **no TLS bypass of any kind**. It gets its own ADR.
3. **A minimal, version-pinned extract of GitHub's OpenAPI description**, holding only the operations and schemas for the endpoints below. It is vendored with MIT licence attribution in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and a recorded source commit and checksum.
4. **Milestone: M3 Reliability.** It does not block M2.
5. **Contract tests that also run against real GitHub,** to detect emulator drift (section 3a).

Scope stays limited to the GitHub endpoints Ilmar actually uses (section 2). An endpoint is added only together with the adapter code that calls it. The emulator supports deterministic fault injection, including **writes that succeed but whose responses are lost** (section 4).

## Goal

Exercise Ilmar's **real coordinator and real GitHub adapters** against a **stateful local GitHub** in CI, with no external credentials:
- an API emulator for issues, labels, comments, pull requests, merges and checks;
- a **local bare git repository** served over git smart HTTP, so fetch, push, branches and commits are real git;
- **deterministic fault injection.**

The real-GitHub and real-Claude-Code live tests (#44, #11d) stay the **final compatibility gate**. This adds a fast, repeatable layer beneath them. It does **not** block M2.

## 1. Can the current adapter safely target a local emulator? (investigated on `main` at a89acb5)

**What already works, without any change:**
- **Origins are configurable.** `api_url` and `git_base_url` are configurable for GitHub Enterprise in `adapters/builtin.py`, through `Options.https_url`. Both must be `https`, with no credentials, query or fragment. A loopback origin such as `https://127.0.0.1:8443` is accepted. Production validation does **not** need to change.
- **The API token stays on its origin.** It goes only in the `Authorization` header to `api_url` (`GitHubClient`). Redirects to another origin raise `CrossOriginRedirectError`, a policy failure that is never retried.
- **The git credential is scoped to one origin.** It reaches git only as `http.<git_base_url>/.extraHeader`, through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables, never argv. It is sent only when `git_base_url` is `https`. A local origin with a port is matched correctly.
- **The protocol stays https.** Git allows only `https` (`protocol.allow=never` plus `protocol.https.allow=always`). `file://` and `http://` stay forbidden. The emulator must therefore be HTTPS, and that is the right test: it exercises the production transport, auth header and redirect handling.

**The one gap: TLS trust.**
- **API client:** `urllib_transport` uses the default SSL context, which trusts the system store. It honours `SSL_CERT_FILE` only implicitly, through OpenSSL's defaults.
- **Git:** `HardenedGit.environment()` builds git's environment from scratch and sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`. So no CA can be supplied, and git would rightly reject the emulator's certificate.
- **Do not fix it** with a test-only flag, by disabling verification (`http.sslVerify=false`, `CERT_NONE`), by allowing `http://`, or by relaxing URL validation.
- **Fix it** with one explicit, production-grade option that GitHub Enterprise users with a private CA need anyway: `ca_bundle = "/abs/path/ca.pem"` on the `github` task and source-control adapters.
  - **Validation:** an absolute path to a regular file that is not group- or world-writable (like the configuration file, ADR-0019).
  - **API:** `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)`, which trusts only that bundle.
  - **Git:** `http.<git_base_url>/.sslCAInfo`, scoped to that one origin, through `GIT_CONFIG_*`.
  - **Never** an option that turns verification off. A test enforces that no such option exists.
  - This touches credential handling, so it needs **an ADR** and your approval (sensitive area).
- **The test certificate:** a throwaway CA and a `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` certificate generated per test session with the `openssl` CLI. No new dependency. If that proves brittle, `trustme` (MIT or Apache-2.0, dev-only) after the licence check.

**Where the tests can run without registering test-only adapters in the production registry:**
- **Default suite (fast, no Podman):** `Coordinator` with the **real** `GitHubTaskProvider` and `GitHubSourceControl` pointed at the emulator, plus the existing fake runtime and scripted agent.
- **Podman job:** the **real CLI** (`ilmar run --once --config …`) end to end against the emulator, with real Podman and the scripted agent image, as `test_coordinator_podman.py` does today.

## 2. Options evaluated

**Endpoints Ilmar needs** (from `adapters/github/tasks.py` and `source_control.py`):
- **Issues:**
  - `GET /repos/{r}/issues` (paginated, label filter), `GET /issues/{n}`;
  - comments: `GET`/`POST /issues/{n}/comments`, `DELETE /issues/comments/{id}`;
  - labels: `POST /issues/{n}/labels`, `DELETE /issues/{n}/labels/{name}`.
- **Pull requests:**
  - `GET /pulls` (head filter), `POST /pulls`, `GET`/`PATCH /pulls/{n}`;
  - merge state and merging, for tests.
- **Checks:** `GET /commits/{sha}/check-runs` (paginated), `GET /commits/{sha}/status`.
- **Git smart HTTP:** `ls-remote` (including `--symref HEAD`), `fetch`, `push`, with Basic `x-access-token` auth.

**A. vercel-labs/emulate** (Apache-2.0, Node; npm `emulate`)
- **For:**
  - fully stateful, in-memory GitHub emulation covering issues, comments, labels, pulls, `PUT …/merge`, refs, branches, commits, contents and check runs;
  - seeded bearer tokens.
- **Against:**
  - its repository content is an internal model: **no git smart-HTTP** and no real repository. Pushes from real git cannot reach it, and its branch heads and merges would be a second source of truth beside the bare repository;
  - HTTP by default; HTTPS only through extra tooling or a proxy;
  - **no documented fault injection**;
  - labelled a "Vercel Labs Experiment", and adds a Node runtime to CI.
- **Verdict:** closest existing fit, but not adopted now. **Revisit when** it can be backed by a real git repository or exposes git smart-HTTP, and offers fault injection.

**B. WireMock** (Apache-2.0, Java or Docker)
- **For:**
  - mature, with HTTPS;
  - request verification;
  - faults: connection reset, empty response, malformed chunk, random data then close, fixed and random delays.
- **Against:**
  - its "state" is a scenario state machine plus Handlebars templating, **not a data model**. Issues, labels and PRs whose contents change with each write would have to be hand-scripted per test;
  - no git;
  - its faults replace a response; they cannot apply a write and then lose the reply (an **ambiguous write**), which is what Ilmar's journal must be tested against;
  - Java runtime in CI.
- **Verdict:** not adopted. Its fault catalogue informs ours.

**C. OpenAPI-driven mocks** (Prism, Mockzilla) on GitHub's OpenAPI description
- **For:** schema-accurate responses.
- **Against:** stateless or random data, and no git.
- **Verdict:** not a server for this. But **GitHub's official OpenAPI description** (`github/rest-api-description`, MIT, updated continuously) is valuable for **contract-validating our fake's responses** for the endpoints above. That keeps a hand-written fake honest. Decided: vendor a **minimal extract** at a pinned commit, with its checksum and MIT attribution.

**D. A minimal purpose-built fake** (stdlib Python, in `tests/`) **plus real `git http-backend`** — recommended
- **One source of truth:** branch heads, commits and merges live in a **real bare repository**. API views (a PR's head SHA, mergeability, merge) are read from it or performed on it with git plumbing (`merge-tree --write-tree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref`). The emulator can therefore never disagree with what git actually did.
- **Real git:** git smart HTTP is served by the real `git http-backend` (CGI), behind the fake's TLS listener and its token check. No new dependency.
- **Small surface:** only the endpoints above, each response validated against GitHub's OpenAPI schemas.
- **Fault injection** at every point Ilmar must survive (section 4).
- **Cost:** a modest amount of test code we own. **Risk:** drift from real GitHub, mitigated by the schema validation and by keeping #44 and #11d as the final gate.

**Decision: D** (approved). It is the only option that gives real git and a stateful API from one source of truth, plus deterministic ambiguous-write faults. A and B can be revisited under the conditions noted.

## 3. Implementation scope

1. **ADR and the `ca_bundle` option.** Rejected options: verification off, `http`, test flags. Unit tests and contract tests.
2. **The emulator** (`tests/github_emulator/`):
   - a TLS server on an ephemeral port, with an API origin and a git origin;
   - per-test tokens, rejecting missing or wrong tokens like GitHub (401, or 404 for private repositories);
   - state for repositories, issues, comments, labels (created on add, like GitHub), PRs (open, closed, merged; head and base from the bare repository), check runs and statuses (settable by tests);
   - pagination with `Link` headers;
   - a test-only control API **on a separate, unauthenticated loopback port**, never on the API origin, for seeding, inspecting, merging, scripting faults and simulating other actors.
3. **Contract validation** of emulator responses against the vendored OpenAPI extract.
   - `tests/github_emulator/openapi/` holds only the operations and schemas Ilmar uses, with the source commit, its SHA-256 and the MIT notice. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` records the extract.
   - A test fails if the adapters call an endpoint the extract does not cover, or if the extract holds operations nobody calls.
   - Updating the pin is a reviewed change.

3a. **Drift contract tests: one suite, two targets.**
   - **One suite** (`tests/contracts/github_api.py`) states GitHub behaviour that Ilmar relies on. For example:
     - issue listing includes PRs, with a `pull_request` key;
     - adding labels creates missing ones;
     - removing an absent label is a 404;
     - `Link` pagination;
     - PR `head.sha` after a push;
     - the merge result and `merged` state;
     - 404 for a hidden private repository;
     - cross-origin redirect refusal.
   - **It always runs** against the emulator, in CI.
   - **Opt-in, it also runs** against real GitHub on the disposable `ilmar-disposable` repository. It reuses the live harness's guard (fine-grained token, 7 days at most, no Administration, Actions, Workflows, Secrets or Webhooks), per-run branches and labels, cleanup and leak scanning (#11d, ADR-0023).
   - **It runs** with `scripts/live_run.py` (or `--only contracts`), before the end-to-end live tests.
   - A behaviour that passes on the emulator but fails on real GitHub is **emulator drift**. The emulator is fixed first, and a regression test is added.
4. **Scenario suites.** Both suites run the full lifecycle (claim, branch push, PR, verification, publish, merge, completion and claim release), each fault class at each endpoint, and crashes:
   - **default suite:** `Coordinator` with the real GitHub adapters;
   - **Podman job:** the real CLI.
5. **Security tests** (section 5).
6. **CI:** the default suite in the existing Checks jobs; the CLI scenarios in the Podman job. Both offline, with a runtime budget. Adding them to the Podman job is a sensitive `.github/` change.

## 4. Deterministic fault injection

A fault plan keyed by `(method, path pattern, n-th matching call, phase)`, where the phase is either *before applying* or *after applying, before replying*. Supported faults:
- **HTTP 429** with `Retry-After`, and secondary-rate-limit 403s;
- **HTTP 500, 502 and 503**;
- **a delay past the client timeout**, and **connection loss** (close the socket without replying, or reset it);
- **ambiguous writes, where the write succeeds but its response is lost:** the emulator applies the change to its state or to the bare repository, then drops or resets the connection before replying, or replies only after the client's timeout. This covers every write Ilmar makes:
  - claim and release labels;
  - issue comments, and their deletion;
  - creating and updating a PR, and the review label;
  - **git pushes:** `receive-pack` completes and the ref moves, then the reply is cut. This exercises `settle_publish`.

  Tests assert that recovery finds the applied change and never repeats it.
- **concurrent updates:** another actor's mutation, injected right before a call. A human removes or adds a label, comments, moves the branch, closes, reopens or merges the PR, or deletes the branch;
- **crashes:** `SIGKILL` of the coordinator at a chosen fault point, as the existing crash suites do. The emulator keeps its state, so recovery is checked against what GitHub "really" holds.

**Assertions:**
- the ADR-0022 invariants: no duplicate pushes, change requests, comments or claims;
- published head = verified candidate;
- nothing overwritten after a concurrent move;
- correct claim release;
- `NEVER_TRANSIENT` failures never retried.

## 5. Security tests

- **Token on its origin:** the token is sent only to the configured API origin. A second "foreign" origin served by the emulator must receive no `Authorization` header, through a redirect or otherwise.
- **Redirects:** a cross-origin redirect from the API (3xx to the foreign origin) is refused and never retried. A redirect on the git origin is not followed with credentials.
- **No leaks:** the token never appears in argv (`/proc` scan during runs), in files under the state directory, in logs or CLI output, in evidence, or in a container's definition or environment. This reuses the leak scanner from `tests/live_harness.py`.
- **Credential isolation:** the token never reaches the agent or verification sandboxes; only the coordinator and git hold it.
- **TLS:** a wrong CA, a wrong hostname or an expired certificate is refused by both the API client and git. A test asserts there is no option that disables verification.
- **Auth failures:** 401 and 403 are policy failures, not retried.

## 6. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Before implementation starts:**
  - read the git-http-backend documentation ([R26], flagged **not yet read**) in primary form;
  - read the LICENSE of github/rest-api-description ([R25]) in primary form;
  - recheck F-027's two unverified assumptions (emulate cannot be backed by real git; WireMock cannot lose a response after a write);
  - update F-027 and the source registry with the results.
- [ ] An ADR for the `ca_bundle` option and the test topology; production URL and credential rules unchanged.
- [ ] The emulator supports exactly the endpoints listed in section 2 (no more), statefully, with responses validated against the vendored, pinned OpenAPI extract (MIT attribution in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).
- [ ] The drift contract suite passes against the emulator in CI and, opt-in, against real GitHub on `ilmar-disposable`, with the live harness's guards.
- [ ] Git fetch, push, branches and merges are real git on a local bare repository, over HTTPS, with token auth.
- [ ] Every fault class in section 4 is injectable deterministically and covered at each endpoint Ilmar uses, including a write whose response is lost (API and git push), with no duplicate effect after recovery.
- [ ] The real coordinator and real GitHub adapters (and the real CLI in the Podman job) run the full lifecycle and every fault scenario.
- [ ] The security tests in section 5 pass.
- [ ] Runs in CI with no external credentials; the five checks stay green.
- [ ] `docs/operations/live-testing.md` states that #44 and #11d remain the final gate.

## 7. Decisions

All approved on 2026-11-05: see the top of this issue. The remaining sensitive-area approvals come at review time:
- the `ca_bundle` ADR and code (credential handling);
- the CI workflow change;
- the vendored third-party extract (MANIFEST §7).

## Sources

- vercel-labs/emulate: https://github.com/vercel-labs/emulate (Apache-2.0; stateful GitHub emulation; no git smart-HTTP or fault injection documented)
- WireMock faults and scenarios: https://wiremock.org/docs/simulating-faults/ and https://wiremock.org/docs/stateful-behaviour/
- GitHub's OpenAPI description: https://github.com/github/rest-api-description (MIT)
- git-http-backend: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-http-backend

## Summary

The issue #29 audit identified this independently testable requirement in Parallel's public documentation: **Responses API statefulness, citations, structured output, and stream compatibility**. The scope below defines the local behavior to implement, with contract tests for full feature coverage.

## Scope

- Mount POST /v1/responses with documented input forms, Bearer auth, model alias, reasoning.effort, previous_response_id, text.format, web_search tools, and stream.
- Map research traces to message/web_search_call items and url_citation annotations with correct Unicode offsets.
- Persist caller-scoped ancestry and handle missing/deleted context explicitly.
- Validate JSON-schema output and documented unsupported fields, with extension hooks for [WS-25](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/55) MCP and [WS-26](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/56) data_sources.

## Solution alternatives and implementation plan

Select a format adapter over [WS-14](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/44)/24 rather than another agent loop. Use ajv/jsonschema and [WS-19](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/47) event adapters.

1. Inspect the existing search registry, transport, server, CLI, and shared JS/Rust types. Define request/output/error fixtures from the linked sources before integrating the feature.
2. Implement the scope through existing modules and the dependency interfaces. Keep external services injectable and optional; default tracing remains off and redacts secrets when enabled.
3. Add the tests below, update types/OpenAPI and installed-package examples, and run existing unit/integration and JS/Rust parity checks.
4. Document supported versions, configuration, deliberate extensions, limits, and external prerequisites. Release only the capabilities covered by contract tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- Current request fixtures work against a local compatible client in streaming and nonstreaming modes.
- Unicode citation offsets reference evidence actually used and schema errors are typed.
- Follow-ups reuse context only within caller scope and missing ancestry returns an explicit error.
- Offline tests use mocks or local servers with finite inputs and test deadlines. Live comparisons are opt-in.
- Existing library/CLI/HTTP behavior continues to pass its tests. Optional dependencies are not required for basic search or capture.

**Status: deferred / not run.** This issue only records future live-test scope. Creating it does not authorize implementation, obtaining credentials, live execution, provider transmission/spending, deployments, standing jobs, permissions changes or backups.

Provide credentials only via an approved secret mechanism, never issue text, commits, logs, screenshots or artifacts; do not collect or expose a key as part of this issue.

Keep deterministic offline, pinned local integration and actual provider-backed evidence distinct. Verify forbidden calls independently and prove at least one relevant invariant fails under deliberate local mutation. No secrets or personal data in evidence. - **File**: `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:57-173`
- **Pillar**: Semantic Traceability
- **Symptom**: `detect_format` (`crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:58-63`, `132-134`) extracts only the terminal file extension via `Path::extension()` (`".json"`) and unconditionally returns `Ok("openapi".to_string())` at line 133 prior to content inspection at line 165, misclassifying cryptographic sidecar files such as `docs/designs/blueprint-01..06-*.digest.json` and `.pipeline/schema-digest.json` as OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 specifications.
- **Test-Target**: `crates/ingest-sysml/tests/code_ingestion_tests.rs`

## 2. Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys)

1. **Why does `detect_format` misclassify `.digest.json` and `schema-digest.json` cryptographic sidecars as `"openapi"` specifications?** Because line 132 checks `if ext == ".json" || ext == ".yaml" || ext == ".yml"` and unconditionally returns `Ok("openapi".to_string())` at line 133 without inspecting the compound filename suffix or JSON payload structure.
2. **Why does line 132 only see `".json"` for compound sidecar filenames like `blueprint-01-core.digest.json`?** Because lines 58-63 compute `ext` using `Path::new(schema_path).extension()`, which extracts only the final dot-delimited component (`"json"`) and discards the preceding `.digest` stem suffix and `-digest.json` filename pattern.
3. **Why does the extension check at line 132 execute before the OpenAPI content check at line 165?** Because Stage 2 (`// 2. Extension-based categorization`, lines 113-137) short-circuits on bare file extensions before Stage 3 (`// 3. Content-based fallback inspection`, lines 139-167) can check whether `content` actually contains `"openapi"`, `"swagger"`, or `"\"paths\":"`.
4. **Why was `.json` treated as an unambiguous indicator of an OpenAPI specification in Stage 2?** Because the detector assumed any `.json` file inside a scanned directory is an OpenAPI specification and failed to account for pipeline-generated JSON metadata sidecars (`*.digest.json`, `schema-digest.json`) co-located in design or schema directories.
5. **Why did existing unit tests in `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:504-546` fail to catch this semantic traceability defect?** Because `test_detect_format_by_extension` (`detectors.rs:511`) asserts `detect_format("api.json", "").unwrap() == "openapi"` with an empty content string and never tests negative invariant probes against `.digest.json` or `schema-digest.json` sidecar artifacts.

## 3. Correctness Analysis

In `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs`, the module safety header (lines 8-15) establishes the core safety invariant that input format classification is a DO-178C / DO-330 TQL-4 preprocessing gate where erroneous format detection causes silent specification corruption or invalid downstream translation.

Tracing the execution path when a cryptographic digest sidecar path (such as `docs/designs/blueprint-01-sysml-ingestion.digest.json` or `.pipeline/schema-digest.json`) is passed to `detect_format(schema_path, content)`:
1. At `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:58-63`, `Path::new(schema_path).extension()` extracts only the final extension segment `"json"`, normalizing `ext` to `".json"`.
2. At `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:66-111`, Stage 1 checks for Markdown extensions or GFM pipe table headers/delimiters. A JSON digest sidecar contains no Markdown table headers or pipe delimiters, so execution proceeds to Stage 2.
3. At `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:132-134`, `if ext == ".json" || ext == ".yaml" || ext == ".yml"` evaluates to `true` and immediately returns `Ok("openapi".to_string())`.
4. The content inspection guard at `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:165-167` (`if content.contains("openapi") || content.contains("swagger") || content.contains("\"paths\":")`) is dead code for every `.json`, `.yaml`, and `.yml` file because lines 132-134 unconditionally return early.
5. Similarly, during directory discovery in `discover_schema_targets` (`crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:349`, `399`, `402-408`) and `find_files_with_ext` (`crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:489-493`), any `.digest.json` or `schema-digest.json` file is matched by `ext == "json"` and routed to `OpenAPITranslator::translate` (`crates/ingest-sysml/src/main.rs:568-570`), violating the **Pure Schema-Driven Classification** and **Semantic Traceability** invariants (`[REQ-0001/detect_format]`).

## 4. UML Diagrams

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as "discover_schema_targets / run_ingestion (main.rs:460)"
    participant Detect as "detect_format (detectors.rs:57)"
    participant PathExt as "Path::extension (detectors.rs:59)"
    participant Translator as "OpenAPITranslator (main.rs:568)"

    Caller->>Detect: "detect_format(blueprint-01.digest.json, digest_content)"
    Detect->>PathExt: "extract final extension"
    PathExt-->>Detect: "returns .json (discards .digest suffix)"
    Note over Detect: "Line 132 matches ext == .json and skips Line 165 content check"
    Detect-->>Caller: "returns Ok(openapi)"
    Caller->>Translator: "translate(digest_content, blueprint-01.digest)"
    Note over Translator: "Misclassified SHA-256 digest sidecar ingested as OpenAPI spec"
```

## 5. Affected Callers / Downstream Impact

- `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:309` (`discover_schema_targets`) -- When invoked on a single `.digest.json` or `schema-digest.json` file with `format_hint = None` or `"auto"`, `detect_format` misclassifies the cryptographic sidecar as `"openapi"` instead of rejecting it.
- `crates/ingest-sysml/src/detectors.rs:349`, `399`, `489-493` (`discover_schema_targets` and `find_files_with_ext`) -- Directory scans for `"json"` collect `*.digest.json` and `schema-digest.json` sidecar artifacts alongside or in place of actual specifications.
- `crates/ingest-sysml/src/main.rs:460`, `568-570` (`run_ingestion_with_code`) -- Dispatches `OpenAPITranslator::new().translate(&content, basename)` on misclassified `.digest.json` sidecars, producing an empty or corrupted `PackageDef` AST from SHA-256 metadata.

## 6. Proposed Correction

<!-- MUST NOT use regex (Check 34: deterministic linear slice/char scanning, no regex crate). MUST be domain-agnostic for upstream crates (Check 19). -->

```rust
fn is_digest_sidecar_path(path: &Path) -> bool {
    let Some(file_name) = path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) else {
        return false;
    };
    let lower = file_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
    lower.ends_with(".digest.json")
        || lower.ends_with("-digest.json")
        || lower == "schema-digest.json"
}

pub fn detect_format(schema_path: &str, content: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let path = Path::new(schema_path);
    if is_digest_sidecar_path(path) {
        return Err(format!(
            "Unsupported schema format for '{}': cryptographic digest sidecar files (.digest.json / schema-digest.json) are not ingestible specifications.",
            schema_path
        ));
    }

    let ext = path
        .extension()
        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
        .map(|s| format!(".{}", s.to_ascii_lowercase()))
        .unwrap_or_default();

    // ... [Stage 1 Markdown and Stage 2 non-JSON extensions unchanged] ...

    if ext == ".json" || ext == ".yaml" || ext == ".yml" {
        let trimmed = content.trim();
        if trimmed.is_empty()
            || content.contains("openapi")
            || content.contains("swagger")
            || content.contains("\"paths\":")
            || content.contains("paths:")
        {
            return Ok("openapi".to_string());
        }
        return Err(format!(
            "Unsupported JSON/YAML file '{}' lacking OpenAPI/Swagger root markers.",
            schema_path
        ));
    }
```

Discovered in audit -- new finding.
