# Open Source Radar — 2026-10-30
_Rotation slot 3 — developer utilities, debugging, testing_

## Executive Summary
Today's slot surfaced four genuinely substantive tools rather than the usual same-day hype wave: a six-year-old, actively-released REST API fuzzer that automates negative-path testing with zero coding effort (CATS); a two-week-old but unusually well-engineered MCP server that gives coding agents black-box observation of any running process via strace/perf/gdb (Debug Anything); a company-backed E2E testing framework that pairs UI-driving with real provider emulation and systematic fault injection (dánwò); and a pytest/Jest-native behavioral-regression tool for AI agents that auto-wraps an existing LLM SDK client (Assay). GitHub keyword search was otherwise dominated by two now-familiar noise patterns: a fresh wave of "time-travel debugging for AI agents" repos (the fourth or fifth independent entrant in this niche since September, all with 0-1 stars) duplicating the already-catalogued OrcaReplay, and a same-day "2026" marketing-title content-farm batch of Roblox/developer-tool repos.

## Today's Best Discoveries

### 1. CATS — 8.8/10
**Decision:** USE NOW

**What it is** — A REST API fuzzer and negative-testing tool for OpenAPI endpoints: point it at a spec and a running server, and it generates, runs, and reports thousands of boundary, type-coercion, injection, and stateful negative-path tests (IDOR, idempotency, update-read consistency, deleted-resource availability) with zero hand-written test code.
**Why I should care** — Negative-path testing is exactly the category that gets skipped under deadline pressure, and CATS is self-healing: when the OpenAPI spec changes, the generated tests change with it, so there's no hand-maintained negative-test suite going stale.
**What it could replace** — Hand-written negative/boundary test cases per endpoint, and the usual gap where positive-path tests pass but nobody checks what the API does with malformed input or already-consumed resources.
**Ways I could use it** — Run a security/compliance profile against a Node/Express or NestJS service in CI; use `cats lint` to catch contract issues before fuzzing; `cats replay --curl` to turn a finding into a reproducible bug report; the `--tui` mode to inspect a long run interactively instead of scrolling CI logs; `--qualityGate` as a release-blocking check.
**Agent opportunity** — Deterministic CLI with exit-code gating and structured JSON/HTML reports — straightforward to hand to a coding agent as a "run negative tests and summarize failures" tool, though it has no MCP server yet.
**Integration effort** — Low: Homebrew or a native binary, point at an OpenAPI spec and a server URL, no code changes to the target API.
**Maturity** — Mature: created 2020, 1,378 stars, 93 forks, Apache-2.0, backed by Endava, still actively released (v15.3.0 shipped the same day as this review), with a documented history of finding real bugs in HashiCorp Vault and Gitea.
**License** — Apache-2.0, no commercial-use restrictions.
**Alternatives** — Schemathesis and EvoMaster (both previously time-boxed out of this catalog as mature-but-generic fuzzers with no stack-specific angle); Dredd; manual Postman/Newman negative-test collections.
**Why this one** — Self-healing zero-code design plus built-in security/compliance profiles and dependency-aware request ordering across endpoints is a more differentiated pitch than the generic fuzzers already passed on.
**Recommendation** — Install and point it at an existing OpenAPI spec as a CI quality gate.

### 2. Debug Anything — 8.2/10
**Decision:** PROTOTYPE

**What it is** — An MCP server and CLI giving a coding agent (or a human) black-box observation of any running process, container, or pod — syscalls, CPU flamegraphs, thread stacks, sockets/fds, packets, heap retainers, container state — by wrapping strace/py-spy/perf/lsof/tcpdump/gdb/lldb/Node's inspector and turning their output into evidence-cited findings, with zero instrumentation or restart.
**Why I should care** — An agent can read every line of code and still have no way to answer "why is this process eating 4GB" — it fumbles the flags for strace, and raw trace output blows the context window. This is the sensory layer most agent-debugging tooling skips, and its evidence-contract design (a finding without a cited evidence id is rejected by the schema) makes the output auditable instead of a plausible guess.
**What it could replace** — Manually running and interpreting strace/lsof/py-spy/gdb output when debugging a hung, leaking, or slow Node/Python process, and the context-window cost of pasting raw profiler output into an agent chat.
**Ways I could use it** — `npx debuganything why <pid> --symptom leak` on a suspected memory leak; "who's holding port 8080" without running lsof by hand; Docker container OOMKill diagnosis; CI hang forensics via the companion GitHub Action; deadlock detection naming the exact blocking lines.
**Agent opportunity** — It is itself agent tooling: one MCP server, 14 tools, auto-setup for Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/Gemini CLI, a proactive hook that nudges the agent toward it on EADDRINUSE/OOM/segfault signals, and Python bindings for LangChain/LlamaIndex/CrewAI.
**Integration effort** — Low: `npx debuganything setup` auto-configures the agent; a `readiness` command reports what's usable on the current machine before any tool runs; no server, no account, no telemetry.
**Maturity** — Emerging: created 2026-10-17, 13 stars, 3 forks — but the engineering (evidence contract, honest per-OS capability matrix, hard resource caps, secret redaction, a Discord community, a documented roadmap) is unusually mature for a two-week-old repo.
**License** — MIT, no commercial-use restrictions.
**Alternatives** — mcp-debugger (already catalogued, USE NOW) and Microsoft's DebugMCP cover step-through debugging — a complementary, different problem (you need to already know where to put the breakpoint).
**Why this one** — No other tool found doing black-box, zero-instrumentation process/container observation specifically packaged for agent consumption with an evidence-citation requirement; it explicitly and correctly positions itself as the layer *before* a step debugger rather than competing with one.
**Recommendation** — Install the next time a Node or Python process hangs, leaks, or won't release a port.

### 3. dánwò — 7.8/10
**Decision:** PROTOTYPE

**What it is** — An E2E testing framework for web/Android/iOS that drives the UI via locators or cached plain-English agent steps, with an opt-in backend layer: emulated third-party providers (Stripe, Clerk, Resend, Google, Slack, 20+ more) behind a proxy, post-test invariants against the database/provider state, and built-in fault injection — `danwo matrix` reruns a test once per fault (500s, declined payments, duplicate webhooks, lost DB commits) and the invariant judges each run.
**Why I should care** — Most E2E setups stop at "did the UI show the right text." The fault matrix answers whether idempotency logic actually holds under a duplicate webhook or a mid-checkout provider 500 — removing an idempotency key from their own demo app and watching two fault-matrix trials turn red (a duplicate welcome email) is exactly the bug class that's expensive to find in production.
**What it could replace** — Manually simulating provider failures (or not testing them at all), and the need for real sandbox API keys for Stripe/Clerk/Resend/Slack/Google just to run a CI suite.
**Ways I could use it** — Fault-matrix-test a checkout or webhook-handling flow for idempotency gaps; migrate an existing Playwright suite incrementally; write a plain-English step once and let CI replay it from a cached recording with no further model cost; test a Next.js + Postgres + Stripe flow entirely offline.
**Agent opportunity** — Ships a skill and MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex; every run produces a flight record (video, steps, calls) surfaced over MCP, not just to a human dashboard.
**Integration effort** — Medium: Node 22.22.3+/24.11.1+, mobile testing needs macOS/Linux plus an emulator or simulator, and the project's own docs warn "APIs will change."
**Maturity** — Experimental: created 2026-10-21 (9 days old), 17 stars, backed by a named company (Carbonme Inc.) with a real docs site and an 8-example gallery spanning Next.js/Postgres/Stripe, Clerk, Better Auth, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, and Flutter.
**License** — Apache-2.0 for the code; the name/logo is trademarked by Carbonme Inc. — standard, not a usage blocker.
**Alternatives** — Playwright/Cypress/Detox directly, which this wraps and extends without the provider emulation or fault matrix.
**Why this one** — No other self-hostable tool found combining UI-driving, real provider emulation, and systematic fault injection with invariant-judging in one framework.
**Recommendation** — Spike it on one checkout or webhook-handling flow; hold off wiring it into a release-blocking gate until the APIs stabilize.

### 4. Assay (assay-evals) — 7.3/10
**Decision:** PROTOTYPE

**What it is** — Behavioral regression testing for AI apps/agents in Python and TypeScript: a pytest plugin and a Jest/Vitest/node:test helper that auto-wraps an existing LLM SDK client, records each test case's tool calls/cost/context against its own last passing run, and separates real regressions from noise via repeated-sample comparison and judge calibration against human labels.
**Why I should care** — A green test suite doesn't show that an agent's *behavior* changed — Assay's own pitch example is one line added to a support agent's prompt making it skip a refund approval step while the final reply still reads fine; `pytest --assay` catches that because it diffs tool-call sequences, not output text.
**What it could replace** — Manually re-checking an agent's tool-calling behavior after every prompt/model change, and the false confidence an output-quality eval gives when the underlying tool-call sequence actually regressed.
**Ways I could use it** — Gate a prompt-engineering PR on behavioral regressions; wrap an existing Anthropic/OpenAI/Vercel AI SDK client with `instrument()` for call-level recording with no manual trace instrumentation; `assay diff` after a model swap; document-extraction regression metrics for structured-extraction agents.
**Agent opportunity** — `assert_called`/`assert_not_called`/`assert_max_steps` primitives are a reusable deterministic pattern for grading an agent's tool usage without another LLM judge.
**Integration effort** — Low: `pip install assay-server` / `npm install assay-evals`, native pytest/Jest/Vitest/node:test integration, no custom trace-emission code needed.
**Maturity** — Emerging: created 2026-09-24 (five weeks old), 23 stars, actively pushed the same day as this review, real published packages on both PyPI and npm.
**License** — MIT, no commercial-use restrictions.
**Alternatives** — whatbroke (already catalogued, PROTOTYPE) covers the same core idea via manual JSONL trace instrumentation instead of SDK-client wrapping; promptfoo/LangSmith remain the output-quality-scoring alternative both explicitly position against.
**Why this one** — Automatic SDK-client wrapping (no custom instrumentation), statistical noise-vs-regression separation, and human-label-calibrated judging (reported via Cohen's kappa) is a more rigorous trust story than whatbroke's manual-trace approach, though the overlap means picking one over adopting both.
**Recommendation** — Try it on one existing agent/support-bot test suite via the `instrument()` wrapper before deciding whether it replaces whatbroke.

## Meaningful Updates
None today.

## Still Worth Trying
Projects flagged USE NOW/PROTOTYPE that haven't been tried yet.
- **Kingfisher** — USE NOW, 8.4/10, first seen 2026-08-30 (61 days ago). MongoDB's own secret-validation scanner (validates against the live provider API, not just pattern matching) — directly on-stack; smallest next step is running it once against an existing repo's git history.
- **AdminForth** — USE NOW, 8.3/10, first seen 2026-09-03 (57 days ago). Generates an admin UI from an existing Postgres/Mongo schema instead of hand-building CRUD screens — smallest next step is pointing it at one existing service's schema to see what it scaffolds.
- **RustFS** — USE NOW, 8.3/10, first seen 2026-09-10 (50 days ago). A permissively-licensed, feature-complete S3-compatible alternative to MinIO — smallest next step is swapping it in for one non-critical dev/staging bucket.

## Small but High-Leverage Utility
**llmock** (piyook/llm-mock, MIT) is a local mock LLM API server speaking the OpenAI, Claude, and Gemini wire formats — fixture replies, Claude-style tool calls, streaming, error simulation, and a dashboard for inspecting exactly what a client sent. Testing AI-agent integration code against the real API means burning tokens and tolerating non-determinism in CI; this gives deterministic, offline, zero-cost responses across all three wire formats in one server instead of three separate hand-rolled mocks. Created May 2024 and still actively maintained (a release shipped the day before this review), it's a two-year-old project with modest traction (22 stars) rather than a weekend experiment — worth a base-URL swap in one existing AI-integration test suite.

## Worth Watching
- **PatilShreyas/debroid** — An autonomous, headless Android debugger designed for AI coding agents (inspect runtime memory, set breakpoints, debug live apps), with real traction (276 stars, actively released). Genuinely interesting architecture, but Android/JVM debugging is off Sourav's core MERN/Node stack — would need a web/Node-facing angle to clear the bar here.
- **mkleczek/pseudogress** — Simulates many virtual PostgreSQL databases to load-test Postgres clients. AGPL-3.0, only 4 days old and 3 stars — too early to assess independently, but a genuinely narrow and useful niche if it matures.
- **arcanemachine/pw-repl** — A Playwright-powered REPL that lets a human and an agent share the same Chrome DevTools Protocol session interactively. Promising "debug together" angle for agent-assisted E2E work, but 1 star and no independent validation yet.

## Rejected / Duplicate Candidates
- **"Time-travel debugging for AI agents" wave** (aakash1552005/rerunner, pomelotea-yuzu/ReBaseAgent, jahnavi-1019/agent-replay, jitendrakumar-ai/time-travel-debugger-mcp, Coisini-cyber/flashback) — the fourth or fifth independent entrant in this niche since September, all 0-1 stars and 0 forks; duplicates the already-catalogued OrcaReplay (PROTOTYPE, 7.6) with no new differentiation. jitendrakumar-ai's tool (SQLite shadow-snapshot rollback for AI-agent file edits, distinct from trace-replay) was the closest to a genuinely different angle but is 1 star/4 days old with no independent signal yet.
- **oimo-ai/apgar** — "Release health for AI agents," thin (4 stars) duplicate of the already-catalogued whatbroke niche with no clear differentiation found within review budget.
- **dajinzhu/mcp-contractlab, nikanjam/docker-doctor, tokyubevoxelverse/bisect** — all single-digit stars, 0 forks, no releases, and in bisect's case no push since July — held out as too thin for a catalog entry this run.
- **Same-day "2026" marketing-title content-farm wave** (dadaibrahim/rogen-cli, manindesguise-source/net-lens-telemetry, teenwolf-glicht/Luau-Utility-Atlas, kanakprajapati7/Sp3ar-Parvus-Dev, albanosz03-wq/Lua-Luau-Syntax-Refinery, Sandeep9026/MrD-Deep-Trainer) — same content-farm pattern flagged on 2026-10-23: near-identical "Best X 2026"/"X Suite 2026" titles, ~50-70 stars each, 0 forks, no real content behind the title.
- **yokomohoyo/insomnium** — a straight fork of Kong/Insomnia with no independent differentiation found; Insomnia itself is already a known mainstream tool.

## Run Notes
Sources used: GitHub Search API (mutation testing, flaky test, time-travel debugging, log tailing, contract testing, git bisect, terminal debugger, test generation, coverage MCP, REPL debugging, API testing, CLI debugger, schema linting, code review CLI, developer tool, self-hosted observability keywords, date-filtered to recent activity), GitHub repos/releases endpoints on 15 shortlisted candidates, raw.githubusercontent.com README fetches for the 5 catalogued entries, registry.npmjs.org and pypi.org for version verification (all matched GitHub release tags where present), hn.algolia.com search_by_date on tags=show_hn for debug/testing/cli queries over the last 14 days (mostly thin personal projects; nothing new enough to catalogue beyond what GitHub search already surfaced). All GitHub API numbers (stars, forks, licenses, dates, releases) verified live via the API per AGENT.md §8, never read off rendered GitHub pages. No source outages this run.

> Filed by `/printing-press-retro` from a run of **Autom** (scorecard 90/100, 100% verify pass).

## Summary

Since the data-pipeline probe was scoped to one declared sync resource (#5364, first released in 4.35.3), `verify` fails every CLI that declares no sync resource. Query-only APIs (search/SERP, validation, screenshot and similar endpoints that need a query and have no collection endpoint) correctly get an empty `defaultSyncResources()`, so they now reach verify verdict FAIL at a 100% command pass rate and shipcheck cannot reach ship. The probe already has a branch for this shape, but it is no longer reachable.

## Where to look

- **Component:** scorer
- **Issue type:** `bug`
- **Likely area:** `internal/pipeline/runtime.go` (`runDataPipelineTest`) and `internal/pipeline/runtime_sync_probe.go` (`chooseDataPipelineProbeResource`)
- **Triggered when:** the printed CLI's `defaultSyncResources()` returns `[]string{}` and neither the manifest (`verify_sync_resource`) nor research.json sets a verify sync hint, in mock or live mode.

## What we observed

verify on a fresh 4.35.4 print of a query-only OpenAPI spec (22 GET endpoints, every search requires `query`; no list endpoint):

```
Pass Rate: 100% (53/53 passed, 0 critical)
Data Pipeline: FAIL: no safe sync resource for the data-pipeline probe; refusing unscoped sync
Verdict: FAIL
```

shipcheck then reports `verify FAIL` while every other leg passes.

In `runDataPipelineTest`, `chooseDataPipelineProbeResource(cliDir)` runs before any sync and returns `"", "FAIL: no safe sync resource ..."` when the declared list is empty (`runtime_sync_probe.go`, the `len(safe) == 0` return). The function then returns `false` immediately. The branch further down that was written for this case,

```go
if mode == "mock" && strings.TrimSpace(cliDir) != "" && !cliHasSyncableResources(cliDir) {
    return annotateDataPipelineProbe(true, fmt.Sprintf("PASS: %d domain tables created (mock mode; no syncable resources declared)", len(tables)), resource)
}
```

can no longer be reached. Both spots are unchanged on current `main`.

The same shape passed before 4.35.3. In the public library:
- `library/ai/serply` (printed with 4.32.5): `internal/cli/sync.go` has `defaultSyncResources()` returning `[]string{}`, and its `.printing-press.json` records verify `data_pipeline: true`, `verdict: PASS`.
- `library/developer-tools/scrape-do` (4.20.0): `defaultSyncResources()` also returns `[]string{}`.

A reprint of either on current `main` should hit the same FAIL.

The documented escape (`source: local-sqlite`, see #4065) does not fit: it also drops live API verification, which is wrong for a CLI that calls a live API.

## Suspected root cause

High confidence: the early return added with the scoped probe treats "no declared resource" the same as "unsafe or undeclared hint". The refusal to run an unscoped sync is correct; turning it into a FAIL for CLIs that have nothing to sync is the regression.

## Suggested direction

When the declared sync resources are empty and no verify sync hint is set, skip the sync step and return a passing detail (e.g. `SKIP (no syncable resources declared)`), instead of FAIL. Keep the existing FAILs when a hint names an undeclared or unsafe resource, and keep never running `sync` without `--resources`. Verify by running mock `verify` on a fixture CLI with an empty `defaultSyncResources()`.

## Acceptance criteria

- positive: a fixture CLI whose `defaultSyncResources()` returns `[]string{}`, with no manifest or research hint, gets `data_pipeline: true` and verify PASS in mock mode, and no `sync` subprocess is spawned.
- negative: a CLI that declares resources still probes exactly one scoped resource; a hint naming an undeclared resource still FAILs; no path runs `sync` without `--resources`.

## Frequency

subclass: query-only APIs (no collection endpoint)

## Complexity

small

## Scope boundary

Does not change sync generation, the local-sqlite classification, or probing for CLIs that declare resources.

## Dependencies

None.

## Related issues

- #5360 / #5364 — prior fix (`extends`): scoping the probe to one declared resource is right; this is the empty-declaration case it no longer handles.
- #4065 — prior retro (`extends`): harvest-built corpora used the `local-sqlite` escape; networked query-only APIs cannot.
- #2488 — open issue (`related-area`): dogfood lacks a live stateful sync→analytics→search pass.

---

body:
## Problem

Retained personal documents and paid transcripts need an explicit deletion owner. Access checks alone do not delete their stored objects/backups or protect shared and formal references.

## User story

As an author
I want eligible personal sources deleted when I request it
So that paid text is retained until then and protected shared examination material is not accidentally erased.

## Scope

- Retain durable owner sources/transcripts without age cleanup. Authorized owner/account deletion targets eligible personal source scope within 24h after prerequisites are satisfied; no additional cancellation grace period.
- Classify ownership, shared/formal bindings and holds before deletion. Execute unambiguous parts and report disputed/ownerless parts pending; do not guess ownership or cascade into formal/shared material.
- Distinguish temporary staging from delivered paid transcripts. Use idempotent DB/object erasure progress and backup removal by actual deletion +30d, with deletion replay before restored content is exposed.
- Closed #775 supplies access-check context, not an erasure implementation. Exceptional historical original erasure has its separate dedicated operator workflow.


### Retention contract

- Initially do not erase personal training history by age or introduce arbitrary organization retention overrides. The owner may delete selected/all personal training history without deleting the account; an active selected training must first be explicitly ended.
- Account deletion erases only the personal training portion of completion history, not non-training examination/results/certificates. Retained formal identity is assignment designation plus participant ID, without contacts, and is readable only under current authority.
- Unambiguous authorized erasure may proceed while unknown-purpose/legacy/shared/held records remain pending classification. Do not guess purpose/ownership, retain everything indiscriminately, or report incomplete erasure as complete.
- Separate personal history, formal evidence, operational traces, capabilities, idempotency, notifications and source objects by approved purpose. The personal-history exception does not silently override every technical/security retention period.
- Initially organizations cannot customize retention periods. Scoped operator holds have reason, end time and audited create/renew/release; ordinary cleanup resumes when no hold remains. A29–A31/D08 technical retention periods and other scoped formal baselines are not replaced by personal-training no-age-cleanup.

### Reviewability

Aim for about 750 added handwritten lines of implementation logic, excluding tests and test fixtures. This is a preferred reviewability guideline, not a hard limit or an automatic split requirement; split only when the resulting outcomes are independently useful, compatible and verifiable.

- Capture exact personal-source deletion identities while owner/dependency evidence is still available, before account deletion nulls owner_id. #850 handles AI transaction/reauthorization; this erasure workflow must not depend on an unbounded in-flight AI lock.

### Owned proof and integration boundary

Own actual retained-source/transcript DB/object erasure and restore protection, consuming #699 classification/receipt contracts. History/result-family mutations belong to #699 and formal result-view authorization to #555/#556; no fake history deletion proves them here. Source tests use real source metadata/progress plus an external storage test double that retains inspectable bytes/generations and can restore an old copy. A deletion-call counter is insufficient. #845 proves the corresponding independent evidence/durability on the selected deployment before activation.

## Out of scope

Implementation of separately owned dependent features, unapproved new policies, unrelated refactors and silent changes to existing quiz/training behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **OUTCOME-01:** Given a deleted account owns a paid transcript also referenced by protected formal/shared evidence and another purely personal source. When run deletion with a storage failure, restart, then restore a backup. Then eligible personal material is deleted once; protected/disputed reference is not destroyed or assigned guessed ownership; restored erased data is hidden before access and backup deadline remains fixed.

- [ ] **ERASURE-SCOPE:** Given Owner deletion would null owner_id; personal and protected formal/shared references coexist. When capture authorized scope before losing owner evidence, crash between stages, then resume. Then persist exact eligible identities and protected/disputed classifications before mutation; no guessing ownerless rows, lost erasure scope or cascade into formal evidence.

- [ ] **ERASURE-RESTORE:** Given A restore snapshot predates actual deletion and its tombstone; the primary disk is lost. When restore with a fake independent evidence port, including unavailable/gapped evidence. Then replay independently surviving deletions before serving; preserve actual deletion timestamps/30-day bounds; fail closed on missing evidence rather than fabricate tombstones. #845 owns selected-installation proof.

- [ ] **PERSONAL-SOURCE-RETENTION:** Given A delivered paid transcript and other authorized personal sources are 13/25 months old; a formal/shared binding and ownerless source are controls. When Run source maintenance, then submit an explicitly eligible owner/account erasure request. Then Age alone deletes nothing. Request deletes independently eligible source data only, preserving protected/disputed bindings with honest pending status. No source reclassification from current quiz title or null owner. History/results are not claimed erased by this source test.

- [ ] **PERSONAL-SOURCE-DELETE-PROOF:** Given Confirmed source erasure with saved scope and byte generations, a second protected object and an old backup. When Delete working source bytes, fail after object mutation before DB checkpoint, restart and restore the old backup against independently surviving deletion evidence. Then Inspect stored bytes/generations and owner reads: eligible content disappears, protected content stays and restored erased content is denied until replay. Preserve actual T/30-day backup bound; missing deletion evidence fails closed. Mock call counts do not establish deletion.

## API changes

Use feature-owned application interfaces, named DTOs and the existing logical OpenAPI group; specify validation, enums/units, nullable fields, auth/ownership, pagination, idempotency and RFC7807 errors with schema-valid examples. New endpoints must be discoverable in /api/v1/api-summary. Prepare exact paths/status mapping before implementation; preserve ordinary existing quiz/training clients. Decision-only work specifies contracts but changes no runtime API.

## Data changes

Identify exact learner/author/organization-owned records and immutable evidence. Use additive migrations and database uniqueness/version guards, bounded metadata comparisons and narrow service transactions. Do not rehash whole documents for version checks. Record retained-reference/cleanup/backfill behavior where affected; this issue does not authorize unrelated destructive cleanup.

## Permissions and privacy

A temporary operator hold against scheduled cleanup does not create an exception to the approved account-deletion outcome. Apply only independently valid protected-reference/erasure-conflict rules; do not retain all personal history merely because a routine cleanup hold exists.

Resolve identity server-side. Check applicable permission, owner, organization/installation, resource visibility and current release independently; default deny for missing/ambiguous context. Do not trust client-supplied subject/scope IDs or log secrets, raw capabilities, private answers or source content.

## Failure cases

Specify validation, unknown-version, stale/concurrent-command, dependency-outage and partial-write outcomes at the owned boundary. Preserve committed evidence and reconcile unknown outcomes before retry; never guess history or silently weaken policy. Offline mutations are not newly enabled; reconnect reads authoritative state and retries use the same semantic identity.

## Observability

Use bounded operation/strategy/version/outcome/latency/lag signals and redacted correlation. Distinguish failure, pending and committed outcomes; audit consequential protected actions where required. Do not put participant/resource IDs, secrets or raw content into metric labels.

## Testing requirements

### Executable scenario matrix

Each scenario asserts the externally visible outcome and persisted side effects. Exercise behavior owned by this issue through its real boundary; use realistic contract fakes for not-yet-implemented consumers. A shared scenario does not move a separately owned feature into this scope.

| ID | Fixture / precondition | Action / fault | Assertions | Smallest useful layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OUTCOME-01 | A deleted account owns a paid transcript also referenced by protected formal/shared evidence and another purely personal source. | Run deletion with a storage failure, restart, then restore a backup. | Eligible personal material is deleted once; protected/disputed reference is not destroyed or assigned guessed ownership; restored erased data is hidden before access and backup deadline remains fixed. | MySQL + fake storage/backup |

- Use plain unit tests for pure rules; MVC/OpenAPI for public contracts; production-compatible MySQL for real constraints, transaction rollback, race winners and restart receipts. Mocks must not return impossible collaborator output.
- At a write boundary, inject failure between authoritative writes and assert no partial outcome; retry after commit/response loss and verify one domain effect. Test stale/conflicting command identities separately from identical replay.
- Cover unauthenticated, insufficient permission, wrong owner/organization/installation and private-resource inputs where applicable. Assert both response and absence of forbidden writes/disclosure.
- For relationship-backed lists/mappers, use multiple parents and children and measure bounded SQL/query count; an EntityGraph annotation alone is not proof. If no JPA read path is changed, state why N+1 is inapplicable.
- External provider/storage/email/payment calls use project-owned fakes/stubs, never real paid services. Use injected Clock for boundaries and restart behavior. Run scoped tests first; broader verification only for affected integration surfaces.

### Audit regression scenarios

| ID | Setup | Action | Required assertions | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERASURE-SCOPE | Owner deletion would null owner_id; personal and protected formal/shared references coexist. | capture authorized scope before losing owner evidence, crash between stages, then resume. | persist exact eligible identities and protected/disputed classifications before mutation; no guessing ownerless rows, lost erasure scope or cascade into formal evidence. | MySQL fault injection |
| ERASURE-RESTORE | A restore snapshot predates actual deletion and its tombstone; the primary disk is lost. | restore with a fake independent evidence port, including unavailable/gapped evidence. | replay independently surviving deletions before serving; preserve actual deletion timestamps/30-day bounds; fail closed on missing evidence rather than fabricate tombstones. #845 owns selected-installation proof. | Integration + independent evidence fake |

### Owned scenario matrix

| ID | Setup | Action | Required assertions | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PERSONAL-SOURCE-RETENTION | A delivered paid transcript and other authorized personal sources are 13/25 months old; a formal/shared binding and ownerless source are controls. | Run source maintenance, then submit an explicitly eligible owner/account erasure request. | Age alone deletes nothing. Request deletes independently eligible source data only, preserving protected/disputed bindings with honest pending status. No source reclassification from current quiz title or null owner. History/results are not claimed erased by this source test. | Source DB + stateful storage fake |
| PERSONAL-SOURCE-DELETE-PROOF | Confirmed source erasure with saved scope and byte generations, a second protected object and an old backup. | Delete working source bytes, fail after object mutation before DB checkpoint, restart and restore the old backup against independently surviving deletion evidence. | Inspect stored bytes/generations and owner reads: eligible content disappears, protected content stays and restored erased content is denied until replay. Preserve actual T/30-day backup bound; missing deletion evidence fails closed. Mock call counts do not establish deletion. | Real source workflow + inspectable external-store/restore fixture |

RETENTION-01..05 history/account/result-view vectors belong to #664/#699/#555/#556. The source-specific cases above replace them here; OUTCOME-01, ERASURE-SCOPE and ERASURE-RESTORE remain real required source integration tests, including capture before owner_id becomes null and no exposure after restore.

## Documentation

- Approved behavior: `docs/architecture/decision-register.md` — `#initial-practice-history-retention`, `#account-deletion-history-scope`, `#retained-non-training-identity`, `#operational-values-and-lifecycle-approved`.
- Architecture/readiness: `docs/architecture/policy-driven-quiz-execution.md`, `docs/architecture/open-questions.md`; issue structure: `docs/github-issue-guide.md`.
- Record API/user-visible behavior and automated evidence in the affected existing documentation. A separate manual-testing file is not required unless directly requested.

- Architecture source context: #472, “Architecture source availability — 23 October 2026”. Paths refer to that reviewed working-tree snapshot; do not substitute an older master document for its approved clauses.

## Dependencies

- Requires #664.
- Requires #699.

Deployment activation additionally requires verified independent deletion-evidence durability/replay for the selected installation, designed in #845. That design is not a prerequisite for local contract/persistence implementation; a local fake is not production durability proof.

## Definition of ready

- [ ] The exact owned outcome, dependency contracts and applicable scenarios below are mapped to the current implementation. Approved product choices are not reopened.
- [ ] Named API/error/permission mapping and additive data constraints are prepared; any remaining gate is explicitly resolved before the affected behavior is implemented.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every owned scenario passes at its named boundary. Contract doubles prove only the stated local assertion; the named integration owner must separately prove real downstream behavior before that capability activates.
- [ ] Interface/port, transaction, immutable-evidence, security, API compatibility and bounded-query requirements are verified where touched.
- [ ] Report what the learner/author/operator sees, with one realistic example and the actual verification results.

body:
### Problem & Solution Overview

The original Bose app offered alarms. OCT cannot wake a speaker with a preset at a given time or switch it off on a schedule.

**Solution:** server-side **scheduled actions** run by an asyncio runner in the OCT process (no cron, no external scheduler). A schedule triggers at a wall-clock time on selected weekdays (or once on a date) and executes an action on one or several devices: **play a preset** (optionally with fade-in to a target volume), **stop**, or **standby**. Run history is kept per schedule.

**Depends on** the issue "Sleep timer — fade out and stop a SoundTouch device after a countdown" (it provides `VolumeFader`, `devices/playback.py`, `SleepTimerService.cancel` and the stateful mock device). **Do not start the runner part (A2) until those files exist on `main`**; if absent, stop and comment on this issue.

### User stories
- As a user I want my kitchen speaker to start preset 2 at 06:45 on weekdays at volume 25, fading in over 60 s.
- As a user I want a speaker to switch off at 23:30 every day.
- As a user I want to see when an alarm last ran, whether it succeeded, and to test it with "run now".

### Decisions (already made — do not re-open)
- **Delivery: three PRs** (overrides the two-PR rule): **A1** (time-zone config, DST resolver, tables, CRUD + validation, `next_run_at`), **A2** (runner, execution, missed runs, manual run, history), **B** (frontend, after A2).
- **Time zone:** add `timezone: str | None` to `AppConfig` (env `OCT_TIMEZONE`). The raw string is stored; a property `effective_timezone` (like `effective_db_path`) resolves: `OCT_TIMEZONE` → else a valid IANA `TZ` environment variable (read explicitly; `zoneinfo` does not) → else `UTC`. It never raises: catch `ZoneInfoNotFoundError`, `ValueError`, `OSError`; values like `:Europe/Berlin` or POSIX strings (`CET-1CEST`) are not IANA keys and fall through; an invalid explicit `OCT_TIMEZONE` logs one WARNING and falls back to UTC. Add `tzdata` to **both** `apps/backend/requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml`. Stored times are wall-clock; changing the zone later moves all alarms. Containers default to UTC unless the user sets the variable (the API and UI show the zone). The field name `timezone` is also read by the support-bundle issue.
- **DST (tested with `Europe/Berlin`):** a function `resolve_trigger_utc(local_date, hhmm, tz) -> datetime` (also used by `next_run_at`): build `naive`; `o_pre = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=0).utcoffset()`, `o_post = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=1).utcoffset()`. If equal → `naive - o_pre`. If `o_pre > o_post` (ambiguous, clocks go back) → first occurrence `naive - o_pre`; the repeated occurrence is never a trigger. If `o_pre < o_post` (gap) → the transition instant: the smallest UTC minute `u` in `[naive - o_post, naive - o_pre]` with `u.astimezone(tz).utcoffset() == o_post`. Required results: Berlin 2027-03-28 02:00/02:30/02:59 → 01:00 UTC (= 03:00 CEST), 03:00 → 01:00 UTC; 2026-10-25 02:30 → 00:30 UTC and **no** trigger at 01:30 UTC; a 30-minute-gap zone (`Australia/Lord_Howe`, 2026-10-04 02:15) → 02:30 local; `UTC` unaffected. Weekday matching uses the local date on which the wall time is specified (Monday = 0, Python `date.weekday()`).
- Device access exactly as in the sleep-timer issue (`DeviceService` live calls; preset = `press_key(device_id, "PRESET_n")`; stop = `stop_playback`; standby = `POWER` only if not `is_standby`). The open PR "fix: add play-preset endpoint with device programming verification" touches preset starting; this issue uses `press_key` and does not wait for it.
- "Preset 2" means slot 2 **on each selected device** (different devices may hold different stations). Members of several devices start independently — not as a synchronised zone; behaviour on zone masters/slaves is unverified (documented). An empty preset slot is not detected (run reports `success`; documented). On some Wave setups preset keys may not start playback (#340 "Wave4 - preset sent from OCT not accepted and started to play") — alarms there may report `success` falsely (documented).
- Tables are created in `_create_schema()` of the schedules repository, which executes `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` right after connecting; version range **450–474** is reserved for later `_apply_migration` changes. Device existence is checked through `DeviceRepository`/`DeviceService`, never by SQL joins.

---

## Part A — Backend

### A.1 Data (A1)
`apps/backend/src/opencloudtouch/schedules/`: `__init__.py`, `models.py`, `repository.py`, `service.py`, `time_utils.py` (resolver), `runner.py` (A2), `api/routes.py`.
- `schedules(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name, enabled, time_of_day 'HH:MM', weekdays TEXT JSON list of 0–6 [Monday=0], run_date 'YYYY-MM-DD' NULL, action 'play_preset'|'stop'|'standby', preset_number NULL, target_volume NULL, fade_in_seconds DEFAULT 0, created_at, updated_at)`. **One-time encoding:** `weekdays == []` together with `run_date`.
- `schedule_devices(schedule_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, device_id, PRIMARY KEY(schedule_id, device_id))` — 0–20 devices; an **enabled** schedule needs ≥ 1.
- `schedule_runs(id, schedule_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, trigger_id TEXT /* UUID per trigger */, device_id, trigger_minute_utc TEXT NULL, started_at, finished_at NULL, status 'running'|'success'|'failed'|'skipped', error_code NULL, detail NULL, UNIQUE(schedule_id, device_id, trigger_minute_utc))`. Manual runs have `trigger_minute_utc` NULL (SQLite treats NULLs as distinct). History is trimmed by **whole triggers**: keep the latest 50 `trigger_id`s per schedule; `running` rows are never deleted.
- `scheduler_state(id=1, last_tick_at)`.
- Limits: 100 schedules (`409 schedule_limit_reached`); name 1–60 after trim.

### A.2 Request/response contract (A1)
Request body (POST, and PUT as **full replacement**): `{name, enabled=true, device_ids, time_of_day, weekdays=[], run_date=null, action, preset_number=null, target_volume=null, fade_in_seconds=0}`. `id`, `needs_attention`, `next_run_at`, `last_run`, `created_at`, `updated_at` are read-only and ignored if sent. Response object:
```json
{"id": 3, "name": "Weekday wake-up", "enabled": true, "device_ids": ["AABBCC112233"],
 "time_of_day": "06:45", "weekdays": [0,1,2,3,4], "run_date": null,
 "action": "play_preset", "preset_number": 2, "target_volume": 25, "fade_in_seconds": 60,
 "needs_attention": false, "next_run_at": "2026-10-26T06:45:00+01:00",
 "last_run": {"trigger_id": "…uuid…", "started_at": "…Z", "status": "success", "error_code": null},
 "created_at": "…Z", "updated_at": "…Z"}
```
- `next_run_at`: first trigger strictly after now, ISO-8601 **with the zone offset**, computed by `resolve_trigger_utc`; `null` when disabled, needs attention, or a one-time schedule is past. `needs_attention` = no devices. `last_run` aggregates the most recent `trigger_id`: `running` if any running, else `failed` if any failed, else `success` if any success, else `skipped`; its `error_code` is that of the first failed (else skipped) device by `device_id`; `null` when never run.
- `GET /api/schedules` → `{timezone, items}` ordered by `time_of_day`, then `id`. `POST` → `201`. `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/schedules/{id}` (`DELETE` → 204 and cascades the history). `PUT /api/schedules/{id}/enabled` body `{enabled}` → `200` Schedule.
- `POST /api/schedules/{id}/run` → `202 {trigger_id, run_ids}` (one `running` row per device inserted **before** returning); manual runs ignore time/weekday/enabled, do not disable one-time schedules, are not subject to the idempotency key; `409 schedule_already_running` if a run of this schedule is still `running`; `422 schedule_no_devices` if it has none.
- `GET /api/schedules/{id}/runs?limit=20&trigger_id=` (`limit` 1–200) → `{items: [{id, trigger_id, device_id, started_at, finished_at, status, error_code}]}` newest first; unknown schedule → `404 schedule_not_found`.
- **Validation (422, `errors[].path` + `code`; all violations are returned together):** `schedule_invalid_name` (`name`), `schedule_invalid_time` (`time_of_day` not `HH:MM`), `schedule_invalid_date` (`run_date` not a date), `schedule_invalid_weekdays` (values outside 0–6 or duplicates; order is normalised ascending), `schedule_date_required` (no weekdays and no date), `schedule_date_not_allowed` (weekdays and a date), `schedule_date_in_past` (resolved trigger ≤ now — checked **only when `enabled` is true**, on create, and on update/enable only when date/time/enabled changed), `schedule_preset_required` (`play_preset` without a number in 1–6), `schedule_invalid_combination` (preset with stop/standby; volume/fade with stop/standby), `schedule_fade_requires_volume`, `schedule_invalid_volume` (0–100), `schedule_invalid_fade` (0–600), `schedule_invalid_devices` (empty when enabled, > 20, duplicates), `schedule_unknown_device` (`device_ids`, on POST and PUT). Others: `404 schedule_not_found`, `409 schedule_limit_reached`.

### A.3 Runner (A2)
Started in the lifespan **before any mock-mode early return** (`app.state.schedule_runner`), stopped in `_shutdown` before repositories close; it runs in all modes. Receives `DeviceService`, the repositories and `SleepTimerService` from the lifespan; `clock`/`sleep` are injected.
- **Tick:** every ≤ 15 s (and on schedule changes); never raises out of the loop. `last_tick_at` is written at most once per 60 s and on shutdown.
- **Eligibility and missed runs, one rule per tick:** compute all triggers in `(max(last_tick_at, schedule.updated_at), now]` (no processing when `last_tick_at` is NULL; if `now < last_tick_at` treat as no gap; lookback capped at 24 h). Triggers within 60 s of `now` are executed; for older ones only the **most recent per schedule** is recorded as one `skipped`/`missed` row per device (others are silently dropped; documented). A missed one-time schedule is disabled. Creating, editing or enabling a schedule never fires retroactively (`updated_at` lower bound). The idempotency guard is the unique key `(schedule_id, device_id, trigger_minute_utc)`, inserted with `INSERT OR IGNORE` in one transaction per trigger with one shared `trigger_id`.
- **One-time schedules** are set `enabled=false` when the trigger rows are inserted.
- **Startup/shutdown:** all `running` rows are set to `failed`/`interrupted` at runner start and for in-flight runs on graceful shutdown (so `schedule_already_running` cannot stick).
- **Devices:** each tick reconciles `schedule_devices` with `DeviceRepository`: ids no longer known are removed (INFO log with schedule and device id); a schedule left empty becomes `enabled=false`. A run hitting `DeviceNotFoundError` → `failed`/`device_removed`.
- **Concurrency:** at most one executing task per device (per-device lock; a task waits up to 30 s, then finishes `skipped`/`device_busy`). Concurrency is bounded by acquiring a global semaphore (5) **only around individual device calls**, never around sleeps, retry waits or fades; retries run inside the per-device task. The per-device budget of 120 s covers wake, retries and key presses and **excludes the fade**, which is bounded by `fade_in_seconds + 30 s`.
- **Execution per device:**
  - `play_preset`: first `SleepTimerService.cancel(device_id)` if a timer exists (a failure is logged, not fatal; this happens **before any volume or key call**). If `is_standby`: `POWER`, poll now-playing every 1 s up to **20 s**, else `failed`/`wake_timeout`. Read `V_prev = get_volume()`; if muted → `set_mute(false)`. With `target_volume` and `fade_in_seconds > 0`: `set_volume(0)` → `press_key PRESET_n` → `VolumeFader.fade(0 → target, skip_if_muted=False)`; with `fade_in_seconds == 0`: `set_volume(target)` then the preset; without `target_volume`: only the preset. If the preset press fails (after retries) restore `V_prev` best-effort. A fade aborted by a manual volume change is `success` with `detail="manual_change"`; on shutdown a running fade-in is cancelled and the volume left as is.
  - `stop`: `stop_playback`; not playing → `skipped`/`already_stopped`. `standby`: `POWER` only if not standby, else `skipped`/`already_standby`.
  - `DeviceConnectionError`: 1 initial attempt + 3 retries 20 s apart, then `failed`/`device_unreachable`. Unexpected exceptions → `failed`/`internal_error` (logged; `detail` is not exposed by the API).
- Run `error_code` values: failures `device_unreachable`, `wake_timeout`, `device_removed`, `interrupted`, `internal_error`; skips `missed`, `already_stopped`, `already_standby`, `device_busy`.

### A.4 Acceptance criteria — A1
1. **Given** `resolve_trigger_utc` unit tests for every case in "DST" above (incl. the day after each transition and a 03:00 schedule next to a 02:30 schedule on the gap day), **then** all pass; `next_run_at` uses the same function and carries the offset.
2. **Given** the time-zone resolution order (`OCT_TIMEZONE` → `TZ` → UTC, invalid values, POSIX-style `TZ`), **then** the tests pass and `GET /api/schedules` returns the effective zone; `tzdata` is present in both dependency files.
3. **Given** each validation code of A.2, **then** a test asserts status 422, `errors[].path` and `code`; a draft with `enabled:false` and a past date is accepted; `PUT /enabled` enabling a past one-time schedule → `schedule_date_in_past`; enabling a schedule without devices → `schedule_invalid_devices`.
4. **Given** the CRUD endpoints, **then** `PUT` replaces all fields, `DELETE` cascades `schedule_devices` and `schedule_runs` (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` proven), the 101st schedule → 409, the list is ordered, `last_run`/`needs_attention` follow A.2.
5. `openapi.yaml` updated; `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` section **"Schedules"** (`OCT_TIMEZONE`, DST rules, missed-run behaviour, limits, known limitations).

### A.5 Acceptance criteria — A2
1. **Given** a weekday schedule 06:45 Mon–Fri, `play_preset 2`, `target_volume 25`, `fade_in_seconds 60` on a mock device, **when** the fake clock reaches Wednesday 06:45, **then** exactly one run row per device exists with status `success`, volume was set to 0 before `PRESET_2`, the fade follows the `VolumeFader` formula to 25; on Saturday nothing fires.
2. **Given** two ticks in the same minute or a restart within the 60 s window, **then** exactly one run row per device exists.
3. **Given** creating/editing/enabling a schedule at 06:45:30 for 06:45, **then** it does not fire.
4. **Given** `last_tick_at = trigger − 1 min` and OCT starting 30 s after the trigger, **then** the run executes; starting 5 min after → one `skipped`/`missed` row per device (and a missed one-time schedule is disabled); `last_tick_at` NULL → no missed processing; a tick stalled > 60 s while running produces `missed` rows the same way.
5. **Given** a restart with a `running` row, **then** it becomes `failed`/`interrupted` and `POST /run` works again.
6. **Given** a device in standby, **then** `POWER` is sent and the preset only after standby ended; a device that stays in standby for 20 s → `failed`/`wake_timeout`; a muted device is unmuted before the fade.
7. **Given** an unreachable device, **then** 4 attempts (1 + 3 retries 20 s apart) → `failed`/`device_unreachable`; other devices of the same schedule are not delayed (semaphore held only around calls).
8. **Given** an active sleep timer, **then** `SleepTimerService.cancel` is called before any `set_volume` of the run; **given** the preset press fails, `V_prev` is restored.
9. **Given** two schedules at the same minute on one device, **then** they execute one after the other; the second waiting > 30 s ends `skipped`/`device_busy`.
10. **Given** `POST /{id}/run`, **then** `202` with `running` rows and `409 schedule_already_running` on a second call; `422 schedule_no_devices` for a schedule without devices; runs filter by `trigger_id`.
11. **Given** a device is deleted, **then** within one tick it disappears from `schedule_devices`; a schedule left empty is `enabled=false` and `needs_attention=true`; a run in progress for it ends `failed`/`device_removed`.
12. **Given** more than 50 triggers, **then** the oldest whole triggers are trimmed and `running` rows survive.
13. Works with `OCT_MOCK_MODE=true` using the stateful mock; all time-dependent tests use a fake clock; shutdown cancels the loop and in-flight fades within 3 s.

---

## Part B — Frontend (after A2)

New page `pages/Schedules.tsx` at route `/schedules` (registered in `App.tsx` before the catch-all; it receives the loaded `devices` as a prop like the sibling pages; with zero devices the existing guard redirects — accepted). Navigation entry via `withDevice("/schedules")` in `components/Navigation.tsx` (position/icon by the designer; other issues add entries too — expect trivial merge conflicts). Hooks `useSchedules.ts`, client `api/schedules.ts`. Visual design by the designer.

### B.1 Functional requirements
1. **List:** name, device names (joined with the devices prop; an unknown id is shown as the id), action summary, time + weekdays (or date), `next_run_at`, last-run status, enabled switch. The server zone is shown ("Times are in Europe/Berlin"). Weekday names/date/time use `Intl` with the active locale **and `timeZone` = the zone returned by the API** (`time_of_day` is shown as-is; the wire format is Monday = 0, not JavaScript's Sunday = 0). While any `last_run` is `running` the list refetches every 10 s.
2. **Enable/disable** inline (optimistic, rollback on error, refetch afterwards since `next_run_at` changes); enabling failures map `schedule_invalid_devices`/`schedule_date_in_past`.
3. **Create/edit:** name; devices (multi-select of known devices, max 20); time (24 h); an explicit repeat mode "weekdays" **or** "one time (date)"; action; preset 1–6 (with the preset's station name for the first selected device from `GET /api/presets/{device_id}` when available, otherwise just the number, plus a hint that the slot may hold different stations on different devices); optional target volume; optional fade-in (only for play preset + volume). Fields not applicable to the action are hidden and not sent. Client validation mirrors A.2 (the server verdict is authoritative, e.g. for "date in the past"); server `errors[]` map by `path` + `code`; `schedule_limit_reached` is a form-level message.
4. **Run now:** `POST …/run`, then poll `GET …/runs?trigger_id=` every 2 s for max 90 s until none is `running`, then show the result (skipped runs show their translated reason). After 90 s stop polling and show "still running — see history"; the list refetch picks up the final state. `schedule_already_running` and `schedule_no_devices` have translated messages.
5. **History:** per schedule the last 20 runs grouped by trigger (time, device name, status, translated `error_code`: `device_unreachable`, `wake_timeout`, `device_removed`, `interrupted`, `internal_error`, `missed`, `already_stopped`, `already_standby`, `device_busy`; unknown → generic with the raw code).
6. **Delete** with `ConfirmDialog`. Schedules with `needs_attention` are marked and offer "edit". Empty state with a call-to-action; loading and error states with retry.

### B.2 Accessibility
Weekday selector is a labelled group; switches expose state; dialogs use `Modal` (focus trap/restore); run-now results are announced via a polite live region.

### B.3 Acceptance criteria — Frontend
1. **Given** schedules from the API, **then** the list shows all fields incl. the zone label; an unknown device id is rendered as the id; with the browser time zone mocked to `America/New_York`, a 06:45 Berlin schedule still shows 06:45 and `next_run_at` is formatted in Berlin time.
2. **Given** a failing toggle, **then** the switch reverts with an error toast; a successful toggle refetches.
3. **Given** action "stop", **then** preset/volume/fade fields are hidden and not in the request body; Monday selected sends `0`.
4. **Given** repeat mode "weekdays" with none selected, or "one time" without a date, **then** an inline error blocks submission; a server `schedule_date_in_past` appears at the date field in the user's language; the 20-device cap is enforced in the multi-select.
5. **Given** run now, **then** the UI polls with fake timers until the runs left `running`, shows the final status; after 90 s it shows "still running"; 409/422 show translated messages.
6. **Given** a schedule with `needs_attention`, **then** the marker and an "edit" action are shown; editing sends `PUT` with the full body; history shows translated `error_code`s and falls back to the raw code.
7. Delete requires confirmation; empty, loading and error(+retry) states exist; the live region announces run-now results.
8. All strings in 10 locales (error codes included); Vitest tests for formatting, validation, polling; Cypress `apps/frontend/tests/e2e/schedules.cy.ts` (create → toggle → run now → delete) with `cy.intercept`.

---

## Out of scope
Per-schedule time zones, sunrise/sunset triggers, arbitrary URLs or non-preset sources, snooze, synchronised zone start, detection of empty preset slots, catching up multiple missed runs, a loudness cap for `target_volume` (unauthenticated LAN endpoints already allow volume 100), hardware verification of standby wake and zone behaviour.

## Additional requirements from discussions (separable)

These requirements were raised after this issue was written. They are **not** part of its acceptance criteria and **may be implemented separately** once this issue and the named dependency are merged.

1. **`select_source` action** — switch the speaker to `AUX` or `BLUETOOTH` at the scheduled time. Source: the Discussion "Feature Request" (wish "Ability to change the Source (Aux, Bluetooth, Presets)" together with daily timers). This issue lists "non-preset sources" as out of scope. Depends on "[Spec]: Play a stream or station now and select the input source (AUX, Bluetooth)" (#556), which provides `DeviceService.select_source`.
2. **Zone target** — an alarm that starts on a saved multi-room group (apply the group, then start the preset on its master). Source: the Discussion "Wake-Up Alarm with Preset & Multiroom Zone Support" ("Target a specific speaker or a multiroom zone"). This issue lists "synchronised zone start" as out of scope. Depends on "[Spec]: Saved multi-room groups with sync mode and repair" (#559), whose `ZoneGroupService.apply(group_id, force=False)` is meant for this use.

## Related issues
- Depends on #535 ("Machine-readable `code` in API error responses") and on the sleep-timer issue #537.
- #261 "Time lag zwischen Remote-Action und Ausführung" — reported ~15 s latency after standby; hence the 20 s wake timeout.
- #232 "Globale Presets wie früher bei BOSE" — preset slots are per device; see the UI hint.
- #302 "Zone Playback via SoundTouch Remote" and #430 "Automatic same-station multi-room grouping" — zone-aware playback is separate.
- PRs "fix(ui): responsive layout, accessibility and wizard redesign" and "feat(frontend): add device bass settings UI" touch navigation/`App.tsx`.

---

## Cross-cutting requirements (apply to Part A and Part B)

- **Prerequisites:** if this issue names a prerequisite issue (marked "Depends on"), **do not start until that issue's PRs are merged** — check on `main` that its files exist. If they are not there, stop and comment on this issue; never re-implement a prerequisite inside this PR (parallel runs would create conflicting copies).
- **Delivery order:** unless the "Decisions" section of this issue defines another split, Part A (backend) and Part B (frontend) are delivered as **two PRs**, A first (it updates `apps/backend/openapi.yaml`), then B (runs `npm run generate:api` in `apps/frontend` and commits `api/generated/schema.ts`). Where the frontend uses hand-written API types (`api/presets.ts`, `api/restore.ts`), B updates them by hand to match the OpenAPI schema. Each PR must pass all gates on its own. Open PRs that edit the same files (responsive-layout/wizard redesign, bass-settings UI, restore-wizard styling, backup-verification) will conflict: rebase on `main` after they merge and keep their markup; never resolve a conflict by reverting someone else's change.
- **Error contract:** failures of new endpoints use the standard `ErrorDetail` body **with the `code` field** from "Machine-readable `code` in API error responses" (#535; `core/exceptions.py`, `core/error_codes.py`). Validation failures list `errors[]` entries `{field, path, message, code}`; **`path`** is the field path relative to the body (`port`, `config.url`) and is what this issue's frontend uses (`field` keeps its legacy form such as `body.port`). Domain codes are raised with `raise_coded(status, code, detail, field=…)` or, for field validators, `ValueError("code:<name>")`. Status convention for new endpoints: 404 not found, 409 conflict/state, 413 too large, 422 validation, 502 upstream service failed, 503 device unreachable (`device_unreachable`), 504 upstream timeout. Never put secrets, stack traces, filesystem paths or raw exception text into `detail`, `params` or `extra`.
- **Backend conventions:** Python 3.11+, async, type hints. Domain modules follow `[domain]/{__init__,service,repository}.py` + `api/routes.py` registered in `main.py` (`adapter.py` only when talking to an external system; routes of an existing domain may stay in its router). SQLite via `BaseRepository`: create tables with `CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in `_create_schema()` (the repositories' pattern); `_apply_migration(version, description, sql)` executes **one** statement and is only for later schema changes in the version range reserved by this issue (versions are global across repositories — grep `_apply_migration(` first). Where `ON DELETE CASCADE` is used, the repository executes `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` right after connecting (it is per connection and `BaseRepository` does not set it; do not change `BaseRepository`) and a test proves the cascade. Register repositories in `repo_classes` in `main.py`, create services in `_init_services` (before any mock-mode early return when the feature must also work in mock mode), stop them in `_shutdown` before repositories close. XML only via `defusedxml`. Datetimes are UTC ISO-8601 with `Z`. New config fields go into `AppConfig` (`core/config.py`, env prefix `OCT_`).
- **Frontend conventions:** React 19, TypeScript strict, functional components, TanStack Query for server state where the surrounding code uses it (note: some existing hooks such as `usePresets` and the Diagnostics page use plain state), `useMutation` for POST actions, hooks in `hooks/`, API clients in `api/`, new pages registered in `App.tsx` before the catch-all (pages sit inside the "devices required" guard), navigation links in `components/Navigation.tsx` via its `withDevice` helper when the issue says so, shared UI from `components/` (`Modal`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Toast`, `EmptyState`, `LoadingSkeleton`). Translate backend failures with `getApiErrorMessage` / `getFieldErrors` ((#535), keys `errors.api.<code>`); unknown codes fall back to a generic message containing the raw code.
- **Design handoff:** the visual design is delivered separately by a designer. Part B specifies **behaviour, data, states and accessibility only**. Implement with existing design-system components so the UI is usable and consistent. If designer mockups are attached to this issue (or linked in a comment) when it is picked up, align the markup with them without changing the behaviour defined here. Do not block on mockups.
- **i18n:** every new user-facing string gets a key in **all 10 locales** (`apps/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`: de, en, es, fr, it, ja, nl, pl, pt-BR, sv). English and German are written properly; the others may be machine-quality but never empty and never left in English, with identical `{{placeholders}}`. The open PR "test(i18n): check interpolation placeholders across locales" adds a parity test — do not depend on it; add key-presence and placeholder checks for your keys to your own tests if it is not merged.
- **Tests / gates:** backend `cd apps/backend && python -m pytest tests/unit/ -x -q`, `ruff check src/`, `mypy src/opencloudtouch/`; frontend `npx vitest run`, `npx eslint src/`, `npx tsc --noEmit`; coverage ≥ 80 %; Bandit-clean. Cypress specs live in `apps/frontend/tests/e2e/*.cy.ts` and use `cy.intercept` (see `tests/e2e/support/`). Time-dependent backend tests use injectable clock/sleep (no real waiting). Reference code by names, not line numbers.
- **Docs:** user-visible behaviour and every new env var go into `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` under the heading named in this issue (GitHub anchors must resolve); add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under *Unreleased*; update the README feature list when the feature is user-visible.
- **Security model:** OCT is a trusted-LAN service (`.github/SECURITY.md`); this issue adds no authentication. Log `scheme://host:port` only, never full URLs that may carry tokens.
